metadata.title: A Bounded-error Quantum Polynomial Time Algorithm for Two Graph Bisection Problems

extraction_notes.note: The iteration bound for stage 1 and its Stirling-based derivation are one sentence, so the argument could not be split into a separate proof node; the claim's statement contains the derivation and Stirling's approximation (eq. 13) is nested as an external theorem.

The algorithm is described stage by stage in running text across Sections 3.1-3.3 interleaved with derivations; each stage is its own algorithm node with unmarked steps, and AP1 is the three-stage overview. Only stage 3 has an explicit itemized procedure (AP4).
Quantum circuits and the example graph are drawn with picture-environment coordinates and two figures are external .eps plots; their content is not extractable.
Probability formulas stated as 'is given by' without derivation: claims with semi_formal rigor rather than plain equations.

the operator $Q$ will denote either the operator $MAX$ or the operator $MIN$, $d$ will denote either $d_1$ or $d_0$, 
$\left| {z_s } \right\rangle$ will denote either $\left| {z_{max} } \right\rangle$ or $\left| {z_{min} } \right\rangle$, 
and $d_s$ will denote either $d_{max1}$ or $d_{max0}$, so,

Q\left( {\left| {c_0 c_1 ...c_{m - 1} } \right\rangle  \otimes \left| 0 \right\rangle } \right) = \left| {c_0 c_1 ...c_{m - 1} } \right\rangle  \otimes \left( {\frac{{1 + t^{d} }}{2}\left| 0 \right\rangle  + \frac{{1 - t^{d} }}{2}\left| 1 \right\rangle } \right),
\end{equation}
